question: A tank is in the shape of a rectangular parallelepiped of size 50 m × 40 m × 3 m. Its capacity in kilolitres is
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of a rectangular parallelepiped (cuboid) = Length × Breadth × Height

Volume = 50 × 40 × 3 = 6000 m³

Since 1 m³ of volume holds exactly 1000 litres (which is 1 kilolitre), the capacity in m³ is numerically equal to the capacity in kilolitres.

**∴ The correct answer is 6,000 kilolitres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the tank (l) = 50 m

Breadth of the tank (b) = 40 m

Height of the tank (h) = 3 m

 

 

 

 50 m
 40 m
 3 m
 Rectangular Parallelepiped Tank

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cuboid = l × b × h

Relation between Volume and Capacity: 1 m³ = 1000 litres = 1 kilolitre

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of the tank = 50 × 40 × 3

⇒ Volume of the tank = 6000 m³

⇒ Capacity in kilolitres = Volume in m³ × 1

⇒ Capacity = 6000 kilolitres

**∴ The correct answer is 6,000 kilolitres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversions for Volume & Capacity

Volume of a Cylinder

Volume = πr²h, where r is the base radius and h is the height.

Volume of a Cone

Volume = (1/3)πr²h, where r is the base radius and h is the vertical height.
